items.summary: The June 17 morning session opens with Lebanon quiet Day 1 confirmed as the overnight's defining signal. Since Trump's June 14 Dahiyeh condemnation and 'don't blow it' warning to Netanyahu, no confirmed new Israeli military action in Lebanon occurred through the overnight cycle. Hezbollah launched no additional drone attacks into northern Israel. Iran's threatened kinetic response to the Dahiyeh strikes — active since June 14 — remains unexecuted through Day 1. The first of two required pre-signing performance tests is cleared. Lebanon quiet Day 2 is now in progress as of the morning session; it must hold through tonight for the primary deal-collapse scenario to remain inactive entering June 19 signing. The analytical weight of Day 1 clearance is meaningful: Netanyahu restraint appears operative rather than tactical. The primary fragility window — Israeli-initiated Lebanon escalation before Geneva — remains open through Day 2 and Day 3 (T-1). Deal structure remains intact: US-Iran MOU declared June 14-15; Trump and Vance virtually signed the agreement on June 15; formal signing ceremony June 19 Geneva; 60-day nuclear negotiation window activates at signing. Iran's 110-day Hormuz closure — which effectively shut down approximately 20% of the world's oil supply — enters its final pre-resolution days. The G7 Évian summit enters its third and final day today. Trump's 'wall not road to a nuclear weapon' framing — distinguishing his MOU architecture from the 2015 JCPOA — has provided the rhetorical scaffold for French, German, and UK partners to absorb the deal. No joint communiqué was planned from the outset; bilateral alignment signals are the operative output. CENTCOM blockade dissolution continues Day 3; US Navy assets repositioning from Hormuz enforcement posture. Iran comms channel Day 16 resolved — diplomatic architecture intact.

items.summary: The session's primary scheduled market event is the FOMC decision at 2:00 PM ET, followed by Chair Warsh's inaugural press conference at 2:30 PM ET. Hold at 3.50-3.75% is the consensus call with approximately 97% implied probability. The rate number is the least analytically interesting element; the consequential outputs are the dot plot and Warsh's inaugural presser. The June SEP dot plot — Warsh's first as Chair — was finalized before the June 14 deal declaration. It will embed an energy-price baseline already being materially revised by WTI's trajectory since the deal announcement. At least Bank of America has flagged at least three members projecting 2026 rate hikes in the dots — a read that will immediately be parsed as a pre-deal artifact, but only if Warsh's presser provides that framing. Warsh has publicly criticized forward guidance and is expected not to submit his own dot entry. His inaugural press conference — the most analytically complex Fed communication event of the 2026 cycle — requires him to contextualize pre-deal projections against a supply-shock resolution pathway in real time, without over-committing a forward rate path. May CPI at 4.2% year-over-year (elevated, energy-driven by Hormuz closure) and unemployment at approximately 4.3% together justify the hold consensus. May retail sales: +0.9% vs +0.5% expected — a resilient consumer signal that reinforces the 'hold and wait' posture. WTI deflationary impulse Day 2: oil markets pricing continued deal progression toward June 19 signing; Brent approximately $84; WTI tracking toward the $78-82 post-signing target range. Oil sanctions waiver on deck T-2 at Geneva signing; Iranian supply re-entry expected to reduce energy CPI pressure within 2-4 weeks of signing — meaning the June dot plot is capturing a peak distortion that is already unwinding. September FOMC is the operative rate-path decision event. The energy-CPI unwind is visible from this morning's vantage but contingent on Lebanon Day 2 holding and June 19 signing proceeding as scheduled.

items.headline: FERC Large Load Interconnection Decision TOMORROW June 18 — Historic Queue Backlog; Federal Judge Reinstates Wind/Solar 5% Tax Credit Threshold; USDOT Grant Deadlines Concentrate This Week
items.summary: The FERC large load interconnection decision is scheduled for June 18 — tomorrow — setting parameters for how large loads (data centers, EV manufacturing, AI infrastructure) connect to the transmission grid, affecting interconnection timelines for gigawatts of committed demand. The grid interconnection queue has grown to historic levels: gigawatts of ready-to-build renewable projects are waiting years for grid connection studies and upgrades; transmission lines for solar and battery delivery require a decade or more from permitting to construction. A federal judge ruled this week that the Trump administration acted unreasonably in eliminating the 5% total cost threshold as a route for wind and solar projects to prove tax credit eligibility — reinstating a prior clean-energy finance pathway. This ruling interacts with H.R. 6938's new nuclear investment provisions and the broader energy-grid modernization framework now authorized under the FY26 appropriations. USDOT grant application deadlines concentrate this week: June 19 (Reduction of Truck Emissions at Port Facilities), June 22 (Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements; Aircraft Pilots Workforce Development; Pipeline Emergency Response Grants), June 26 (Port Infrastructure Development Program). IIJA-funded projects — EV charging infrastructure, smart highways, intelligent traffic systems — continue deployment, requiring new power and data connections against the backdrop of the interconnection queue backlog. The post-deal energy price outlook (Iranian oil re-entry within 2-4 weeks of June 19 signing) will alter investment calculus for grid expansion projects tied to energy cost assumptions.

items.headline: Pacific Northwest Ocean Observatories Dismantling — Newport OR ~11 Days; Washington Station Already Removed; Cascadia Subduction Zone Real-Time Monitoring Degrading
items.summary: The Trump administration has directed removal of ocean observatories from Pacific Northwest coastal waters. The Oregon coastal station operated by NSF's Ocean Observatories Initiative (OOI) at Newport is approximately 11 days from removal — with full pull expected before end of June 2026. The Washington state offshore station has already been removed. These observatories provided real-time monitoring of Cascadia Subduction Zone seismic activity, ocean temperature and chemistry data, and early-warning infrastructure for tsunami precursors. Their removal creates a scientific monitoring gap in the highest-risk subduction zone in North America — a zone scientists project could generate a magnitude 9.0+ earthquake and 100-foot tsunami within the next 50 years. OPB reported the removal on June 4; scientific community response has been sharply critical. No replacement monitoring infrastructure has been announced. The observatory dismantling is a compounding PNW infrastructure-risk factor alongside the active wildfire emergency and drought conditions.

items.headline: Oregon Wildfire Emergency ACTIVE — EO 26-10 Day 2; 414 Fires YTD, 8,000+ Acres; Oregon 83% Drought; Above-Normal Fire Potential OR/WA/ID Through August; Extreme Heat Warning Active Through Midnight; Heat Mortality Lag Window OPEN
items.summary: Oregon Governor Tina Kotek's Executive Order 26-10, signed June 15, declared a wildfire state of emergency for the entire state — entering Day 2 this morning. The declaration activates all available firefighting resources: aerial support, ground crews, emergency personnel, and the Oregon Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan. The EO remains in effect through end of October 2026 or fire season end. Context: Oregon has experienced 414 fires this season through mid-June, burning more than 8,000 acres with multiple evacuations already conducted. The US Drought Monitor (June 4) showed drought covering 83% of Oregon — near-record low snowpack entering the season. NIFC projects above-normal wildfire potential for all of Oregon, Washington, and Idaho through August, driven by El Niño warmth residuals, heavy spring grass growth as standing fuel, and below-normal snowpack. Washington is in its 4th consecutive drought year (Day 13 of active monitoring window). Eastern Washington grassland fuel moisture levels are critically low — elevated ignition risk across eastern Oregon and Washington concurrent with the wildfire emergency declaration. Extreme heat warning remains active through midnight June 16-17 in Seattle metro and eastern Washington; temperatures peaked at 95-100°F on June 16. The 24-48 hour heat mortality lag window is open this morning — the primary period for heat-related hospitalization and mortality reporting from yesterday's peak. BPA hydropower demand remains elevated with air conditioning load at peak. Pacific Power is implementing proactive wildfire risk reduction: power-line de-energization protocols (PSPS) expected in high-risk conditions this week across its Oregon and Washington service territory.
